heading: A family remembered by Lucy Mack Smith
introduction: Lucy Mack Smith told her family’s story in 1844 and 1845, looking back across decades of work, illness, faith and loss. Let us follow ten of the moments she remembered, and meet the people whose love helped sustain Joseph.

stories.heading: Praying beside their daughter
paragraphs: A fever swept through the Smith household in Lebanon, New Hampshire. As Sophronia grew dangerously weak, Lucy and Joseph Sr. knelt beside her bed and prayed. Lucy remembered gathering her daughter into her arms and watching anxiously as her breathing returned.
Their faith took the form of staying close. Before we meet Joseph as a preacher or translator, we meet a family learning to carry fear together and to turn toward God while caring for one another.

image.alt: Lucy and Joseph Sr. kneel beside their daughter’s bed in prayer.

stories.visitor_caption: Lucy and Joseph Sr. pray beside Sophronia during the illness that swept through their household in Lebanon.

stories.heading: A brother keeps watch
paragraphs: During Joseph’s long illness, Hyrum offered to take his exhausted mother’s place beside the bed. Lucy remembered him holding Joseph’s painful leg for hours, trying to ease his younger brother’s suffering.
Joseph was about seven; Hyrum was twelve or thirteen. The devotion we later see between these brothers began in the ordinary courage of a child who would not leave his brother alone.

image.alt: Young Hyrum sits beside Joseph’s bed, gently supporting his brother’s covered leg.

stories.visitor_caption: Hyrum keeps watch beside Joseph, taking his weary mother’s place and trying to ease his brother’s pain.

stories.heading: A mother’s faith travels with her daughter
paragraphs: Before Lucy followed her husband to Palmyra, she said farewell to her mother, Lydia Gates Mack. Lydia encouraged her daughter to remain faithful and spoke of the hope that they would meet again beyond this life.
The move carried more than household belongings westward. Lucy took with her a mother’s counsel and a hope in God that would become part of the spiritual life of her own children.

image.alt: Lucy Mack Smith embraces her elderly mother, Lydia, at a doorway.

stories.visitor_caption: Before leaving for Palmyra, Lucy says farewell to her mother. Lydia’s counsel carried the hope that faith and family bonds would reach beyond this life.

stories.heading: Gathering to listen
paragraphs: Lucy remembered the family drawing together in the evenings to listen as Joseph spoke about what he had learned. Parents, older siblings and younger children shared the room and gave their attention to him.

These conversations belonged to family life before the Church was organized. Listening, asking and returning to the conversation together helped them face changes whose full meaning they could not yet see.

image.alt: Joseph speaks to his family as they gather around him by candlelight.

stories.visitor_caption: The Smith family gathers to listen to Joseph. Lucy remembered evenings when parents and children shared these conversations.

stories.heading: Alvin’s charge to his family
paragraphs: As Alvin approached death, he spoke to his brothers and sisters about the responsibilities they would carry after him. He asked Hyrum to finish the house for their parents, encouraged Sophronia to be kind to them, and urged Joseph to remain faithful and set a good example for the younger children.
Alvin died on 19 November 1823, at twenty-five. His counsel joined faith to practical duties: finish the work, care for your parents and help those who are younger than you.

image.alt: Hyrum holds Alvin’s hand and listens beside his bed.

stories.visitor_caption: Hyrum listens beside Alvin’s bed. Alvin asked his family to care for their parents, finish the work before them and remain faithful.

stories.heading: Waiting through the night
paragraphs: After Joseph asked about a chest with a lock and left with Emma, Lucy waited through the night in prayer. Morning brought the familiar work of preparing breakfast, but her thoughts remained with her son.
Her account lets us pause with the mother who waited while the events of the Restoration unfolded beyond her sight. Prayer and daily work stood beside one another in her care for Joseph.

image.alt: Lucy Mack Smith prays alone in the quiet hours before dawn.

stories.visitor_caption: Lucy waits in prayer through the night after Joseph and Emma leave, carrying her concern for her son into the morning’s work.

stories.heading: Hyrum comes when he is needed
paragraphs: When Don Carlos brought the message that Joseph needed a chest, Hyrum emptied one and carried it to him. Lucy’s history gives this practical act a place in the story of protecting the plates.
We can see Hyrum’s loyalty in the weight he was willing to carry. He responded to his brother’s need with something useful, and he went without delay.

image.alt: Hyrum carries a wooden chest toward the doorway, ready to help Joseph.

stories.visitor_caption: Hyrum emptied a chest and carried it to Joseph after Don Carlos brought word that it was needed.

stories.heading: A mother speaks of mercy
paragraphs: After Martin Harris reported the manuscript missing, Joseph was overwhelmed with grief. Lucy tried to comfort him with the hope that repentance could bring forgiveness.

She did not make the loss small. She helped her son look beyond despair toward God’s mercy. In this moment, the family story invites us to consider how we speak to someone who knows that a serious mistake has been made.

image.alt: Lucy sits close to Joseph and speaks with compassion as he looks toward her.

stories.visitor_caption: After the manuscript loss, Lucy offers Joseph the hope that repentance can bring forgiveness.

stories.heading: A son’s joy at his father’s baptism
paragraphs: Lucy remembered Joseph’s tears of joy after his father was baptized. He leaned against his father and wept, grateful to see him take this step of faith.
The Restoration was also a family’s religious journey. For Joseph, this was a moment to hold his father close and rejoice in a commitment to Jesus Christ.

image.alt: Joseph embraces his father beside the water after his father’s baptism.

stories.visitor_caption: Joseph holds his father close after his baptism on 6 April 1830. Lucy remembered her son’s tears of joy.

stories.heading: The care comes home
paragraphs: After Joseph Sr.’s death, Lucy injured her knee and became ill. She remembered weeks in which family members kept watch through the nights, and she named the devoted care of Sophronia, Arthur Millikin and her youngest daughter, Lucy.

The mother who had watched beside sick children now received their care. Here the family story brings us back to the love that crosses generations, and to Lucy’s gratitude for the people who stayed near through a difficult season.

image.alt: Lucy’s youngest daughter tends to her mother, drawing a cover across her lap.

stories.visitor_caption: The care Lucy once gave her children returns to her. Her family kept watch and helped her through illness after her husband’s death.
